lines: Restitution is not a word. It is what you do next.
Then settle it plainly. Pay, bargain honestly, walk away worse, or make a threat you cannot take back.
If you want this repaired, choose how you mean to repair it.
You caused the harm. Now decide what kind of person you are afterward.
This does not mend itself. Choose your answer carefully.
Payment, a fair bargain, refusal, or threat. Each one says something about you.
The village is listening now. Make your choice with that in mind.
You can still handle this cleanly, but not by standing there silent.
Repair starts with what you do next, not what you wish had happened.
Choose plainly. This moment is already <pulse>heavy</pulse> enough.
If you mean to make amends, say so and back it with action.
Your next answer decides whether this ends as a mistake or an insult.
No one here can choose for you.
The damage is done. What matters now is whether you face it.
You have four ways forward, and silence is not one of them.
Speak honestly, even if the answer is ugly.
I am giving you a chance to put this right.
Do not reach for excuses. Choose what you will actually do.
There is still a clean way out of this.
The village wants an answer before tempers get worse.
Fine. Not free, but less. Pay {payment_count} {payment_items} and this can end cleanly.
I will lower it this once. {payment_count} {payment_items}. Do not make me regret the mercy.

{payment_count} {payment_items}. That is the <pulse>reduced</pulse> amount, and it is final.

All right. The new amount is {payment_count} {payment_items}.

Bring {payment_count} {payment_items} and we can close this.
I would rather recover part of the cost than prolong the argument.
This is the only reduction I will offer.
The village can accept {payment_count} {payment_items} without calling the debt ignored.
I am agreeing because you bargained in good faith.
Pay the smaller amount now, before either of us reconsiders.
No. The amount stands. Do not spend trust you have not earned.
No bargain. Pay what was asked or choose another answer.
You opened the problem. You do not get to name its whole price.
No. This is not a market stall, and I am not haggling over harm.
The cost stands. You can pay it, refuse it, or make this worse.
I will not lower the price just because regret arrived late.
No. A fair repair does not shrink because it is inconvenient.
The amount is already plain. Do not make me repeat it colder.
You do not bargain down trust after breaking it.
<shake>No.</shake> The payment stays as it is.
Your argument changes nothing.
I heard you. The answer is still no.
The repair costs what it costs.
Someone else should not lose out because you dislike the price.
You can object, but the amount will not move.
This is compensation, not a favor I am selling.
There is no smaller payment that makes the damage right.
I will discuss how you pay, not whether the debt is real.
Stop bargaining and decide whether you mean to settle.
The village has already named the fair amount.
Fine, here is {payment_count} {payment_items}
I will pay {payment_count} {payment_items}
Take the {payment_count} {payment_items}
Here. This should settle it
I will make this right
Fine. I will pay what I owe
Take it. I want this settled
Here is the payment
I will cover the cost

Payment accepted. Next time, permission comes first.
That covers the damage. It does not erase the lesson.
Good. Let this be the end of the mistake, not the start of another.
The payment is accepted. The village will remember that you chose repair.
That makes the account even enough to close.
Fine. This matter rests, but the memory stays useful.
You paid what was owed. Now do better with what remains.
That is enough for restitution.
Payment accepted. Let this end <pulse>cleanly</pulse>.
The debt is paid. Leave the matter closed.
I will tell the others that you made good on the damage.
This covers the repair and the lost supplies.
You chose the responsible answer.
The village can work with an honest payment.
We are even on the cost, though trust will take longer.
I have counted it. Nothing more is owed today.
The damaged property can be replaced now.
You stayed and accepted responsibility. That matters.
We can end the argument here.
You do not have {payment_count} {payment_items}. Then choose another answer.

Empty hands cannot settle this payment. Choose again.
You cannot pay with what you do not have.

Come back with the full amount if payment is your answer.

You offered {payment_count} {payment_items}, and that is what this requires.
Choose another answer if you cannot cover the cost.
There is not enough here to call the debt settled.
Do not hand me less and hope I fail to notice.
The agreed payment must be complete.
You will need to find the missing items or change your choice.
Then you choose the harder memory.
Refusal is an answer. The village will remember it.
So be it. You leave this worse than you found it.
Then there is nothing clean about this ending.
You had a chance to repair this. You chose not to.
Fine. Refusal has its own cost.
Do not act surprised when this follows you.
The village offered a way to settle it. You refused.
Then the debt stays where everyone can see it.
<shake>So be it.</shake> The village will remember.
Then leave, and understand why the doors close behind you.
I will tell the village that you rejected every chance to repair this.
You are free to refuse. We are free to remember.
That answer ends the discussion, not the debt.
Do not expect ordinary trust after this.
You had a fair choice and turned away from it.
We will repair the damage without your help.

Go. There is nothing more to settle with words.
This could have ended differently.
Then we are past words.
A threat answers the question clearly enough.
You chose force. The village heard you.
That is the answer of someone with nothing better left.
So this is what you bring instead of repair.
A threat does not make the debt smaller. It makes you smaller.
Then every door here has reason to close.
You could have settled this. You chose fear instead.
The village knows what your apology is worth now.
<shake>Careful.</shake> You just made this much worse.
Do not threaten people whose property you already damaged.
The guards will hear about that answer.
You were offered a peaceful way through this.
Back away before the village treats you as an active danger.
That threat will outlast any apology you offer later.
You have turned a debt into a question of safety.
Nobody here is frightened into forgetting what happened.
Leave now if violence is the only answer you have.
The village will prepare for your return.
You have made your intentions plain.
That is enough. Next time, ask before reaching.
Reduced or not, the payment is accepted. Do better next time.

Fine. The reduced payment closes this matter.
That will do. Mercy was part of the price, so do not waste it.
Accepted. Remember that this was lowered, not forgotten.
The bargain is settled. Let the lesson stay with you.
That payment is enough to end this cleanly.
Good. You met the bargain. Now meet the expectation.
Reduced payment accepted. Keep your hands <pulse>honest</pulse> next time.
I have counted the reduced amount. We are done.
The smaller payment is enough because we agreed to it.
You kept the bargain, and I will keep mine.
This closes the debt at the amount we settled on.
The village accepted less. Remember that kindness.
Your payment matches the new terms.
I will mark the account paid.
We found a fair compromise and you honored it.
Nothing more is due under this bargain.
Take the second chance seriously.
